summary: Iteration 8 backend testing: All 37 tests pass (27 regression + 10 new iteration 8 tests). Verified susun tokens shape, susun grading with mixed correct/wrong answers, SM-2 spaced repetition progression + quality=0 reset, due-cards endpoint + auth gating, jukugo LLM padding for chapter 2 (admin-only), bunpo answer no-leak, and /api/chapters BabPicker regression (49 chapters with required fields).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~1040 lines — approaching the 700-line guidance threshold. Consider splitting into routers (auth, chapters, admin, library, sr) as the file continues to grow.

jukugo pad endpoint silently swallows LLM exceptions (except Exception: continue) which is intentional per spec, but no error count is returned in the response — consider adding a 'failed' count for observability.
_sm2_update: when reps>=3 and prev interval==0 (edge case if data was mutated), `round(0 * ease) or 1` gracefully returns 1 — good. Formula matches SM-2 correctly.

/api/library/due-cards silently drops cards whose source content no longer resolves (chapter unpublished / kanji removed). Consider surfacing this in a 'missing' count so learners don't have stale review debt hidden.
card_reviews collection uses composite unique index (user_id, card_id) — correct. Missing TTL: old reviews accumulate forever.
seed_data_creation: Test learner accounts registered per test module (TEST_iter8_* prefix). One SM-2 card_review record created for card_id='kanji|26|遅' on the iter8 learner. Chapter 2 kanji jukugo were extended via LLM (persistent side effect).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 8 tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration8.py (10 tests). All 37 backend tests pass. pytest.ini pins -n 2 --dist loadscope; run with REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL env var exported. Chapter 2 jukugo lists are now padded (LLM side effect from test_pad_jukugo_chapter_2) — the endpoint is idempotent (skips kanji already at >=4 examples). For SM-2, the review test leaves a card in the iter8 learner's card_reviews collection; each new test-run creates a fresh learner so no cross-run pollution.
